audit.reasoning: The record has no quotation of its own; it points to an internal adjudication note whose deciding text is StressTyp2's digest of Abas & Grimes 1995, confirmed verbatim in the held StressTyp2 dump but never checked against the primary. That is a second-hand source for a language with a 332-pp modern reference grammar (Hanson 2003) and a dedicated CAD chapter, neither held. Nothing suggests the DOMINANT coding is wrong: the two primaries fetched sources now both support it -- Matthes 1875 sec. 44-45 (pp. 26-28, read first-hand from the MDZ scan) gives penult 'doorgaans' for native words, antepenult precisely in the class of trisyllables ending in a non-nasal 'sharp' (checked/echo) vowel, and categorical shift to the syllable before a suffix, which matches the StressTyp2 passage and vindicates StressTyp2 note 721's reading of Matthes; Grimes & Grimes 1987 p. 96 states penult as the South Sulawesi norm. So: keep fixed-d

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Barbara D. Grimes. 1987. Languages of South Sulawesi. Pacific Linguistics D-78. Canberra: ANU. (from sealang.net PL archive)
sources.quote: 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable.' Family-level statement covering the Bugis dialect wordlists; only Selayar is singled out for antepenultimate deviations.
